work.title: Tesla
work.subtitle: Manufacturing controls engineering intern
work.desc: Summer 2026 on a manufacturing controls team in Austin: Siemens PLC and HMI work, and an AI platform that helps engineers debug equipment.
work.summary: A summer on a manufacturing controls team at Tesla in Austin. I split the time between the controls themselves (Siemens PLC and HMI software, interlocks, fail-safe behavior, commissioning and troubleshooting on the line) and the tools around them: an AI engineering platform, its evaluations and a dashboard that help engineers find and fix equipment problems. Production numbers and equipment specifics stay with Tesla.

highlights.title: An AI platform for the controls team
highlights.text: A Python and C++ platform that takes in the team's documentation, searches it by meaning, and keeps labeled debugging traces and graphs of how the systems connect. It supports code generation, fault classification, schematic tracing and incident diagnosis.

highlights.title: Testing the AI before it is trusted
highlights.text: Versioned evaluations check generated code against how the equipment should behave and its safety constraints, and safety-critical changes go through human review. They caught wrong fault diagnoses and generated changes that left out required interlocks, and those results shaped the next revisions of the platform.

highlights.title: A dashboard for the line
highlights.text: An AI-assisted dashboard that flags abnormal production trends and recurring process faults, and puts the metrics and equipment context beside each flag so engineers can look into possible safety issues.

highlights.title: PLC and HMI software
highlights.text: I wrote and commissioned Siemens S7-1500 PLC and HMI software in TIA Portal, in SCL, ladder and function block diagram: process interlocks, operator workflows, fail-safe controls, multi-axis sequencing, debounce logic and torque control for equipment running in real time.

highlights.title: One interface across the lines
highlights.text: I designed and documented reusable PLC/HMI interfaces and integration specifications: where direct writes or a cyclic abstraction fit, how HMI and IPC network addresses map across several production lines, and a standard way to control the equipment.

highlights.title: Plant integrations
highlights.text: I built and debugged the APIs and sign-in links between plant systems (REST services, single sign-on, RFID badge authentication and identity mapping), and reverse-engineered legacy binaries to trace failures that kept coming back across connected systems.

highlights.title: Machine-vision inspection
highlights.text: I helped commission, calibrate and validate camera-based inspection systems in battery manufacturing, comparing production images against the CAD design and checking parts for defects.

highlights.title: Finding the root cause
highlights.text: When equipment went down I worked with electrical, mechanical, controls and network engineers to find out why, from PLCs, remote I/O, HMIs and industrial networks to safety circuits, power, sensors, cabling and cameras, using schematics, PLC diagnostic buffers, watch tables and live tests.

work.title: 4D Mapping
work.subtitle: Object detection and AI optimization
work.desc: A computer-vision workbench I built: put in an ordinary 2D video and it finds the objects, tracks them and rebuilds the scene in 4D, which is x, y and z plus time.
work.summary: A plain 2D video goes in. Object detection finds the subject in every frame, depth models and camera solving lift each frame into 3D, and the frames are joined into one scene you can orbit and scrub through time. Earlier positions stay in the scene as ghosts, so a deer's whole path through the woods shows at once. The demo below comes out of my own pipeline from a single clip, with no 3D scanner and no extra cameras.

highlights.title: Space and time from one video
highlights.text: One ordinary video is enough: the camera's path is solved, the subject is tracked frame by frame, and the whole scene is placed in x, y, z and time.

highlights.title: Detection, measured
highlights.text: On a 1,000-image hold-out set, RF-DETR large finds people at 0.878 AP@0.50 in 35 ms a frame on an M5 Max, against 0.489 for the small model that runs on the device.

highlights.title: What the stock detectors miss
highlights.text: For subjects such as a deer, open-vocabulary detection and segmentation (Grounding DINO and SAM) find them and cut them out.

highlights.title: The photoreal version
highlights.text: Gaussian splats and per-frame 3D Gaussians, trained on the real frames and scored on frames held out from training.

highlights.title: No one in the loop
highlights.text: Drop a clip in a folder and the pipeline runs end to end and writes its own report.

highlights.title: Its own app
highlights.text: A native desktop app in Rust on wgpu: a 4D timeline, orbit, top-down and follow cameras, and manual correction of detections.

work.title: ThinkFree Finance
work.subtitle: Founder and software engineer
work.desc: An AI platform I founded that turns financial news and public records into plain-English explanations, with every number checked against its source.
work.summary: ThinkFree Finance explains markets for people who don't follow them for a living: renters, hourly workers, small-business owners, students. It reads the news, links it to public records and writes plain-English reports. A language model can state a wrong number as confidently as a right one, so the pipeline checks what it can and labels what it can't.

highlights.title: The news pipeline
highlights.text: News is collected, clustered by embeddings and summarized by a language model, with FAISS retrieval over economic reference texts; it's built to process over 1,000 articles a day.

highlights.title: Following the money
highlights.text: It links politicians, bills, lobbying, congressional trades and public spending, using SEC EDGAR, OpenFEC, USASpending, BLS, Census and other public sources.

highlights.title: Checking the numbers
highlights.text: Numbers in generated reports are checked against the source data, and a summary that fails the check is withheld.

highlights.title: Website and app
highlights.text: A FastAPI website with accounts, MFA, CSRF protection, role-based access and a hash-chained audit log, plus a SwiftUI iPhone app.

highlights.title: My own security review
highlights.text: In October 2026 I ran my own security review and logged every bug I found with the test that proves the fix.

work.title: hardcaml-pwm
work.subtitle: Digital hardware design in OCaml
work.desc: A rotary-encoder knob that sets a PWM duty cycle, written in Jane Street's Hardcaml. The duty glides to each new value instead of jumping.
work.summary: A small piece of digital hardware written in OCaml with Jane Street's Hardcaml. Turn a rotary encoder and a PWM output follows, sliding to the new duty cycle over a few periods instead of jumping there. Simulated and tested, with the Verilog generated; a learning project that hasn't been run on an FPGA board yet.

highlights.title: A PWM that glides
highlights.text: Each new duty-cycle target ramps in over a fixed number of periods and lands exactly, with no rounding error.

highlights.title: Reading the encoder
highlights.text: A quadrature decoder for an EC11-style rotary encoder: synchronizers, debouncing, direction from the A and B edges, and a click only on a real detent.

highlights.title: Tested in simulation
highlights.text: Every block has waveform tests in simulation, and the Verilog is generated from the OCaml.
